LESSON: WRITING 10.4.1 PUNCTUATION (THE EXCLAMATION MARK)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Writing 10.4.1 Punctuation (The exclamation mark)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 10.4.1 Punctuation (The exclamation mark), part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do you think it is important to use the exclamation mark when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. recognise the exclamation mark from writings on wall charts/ board/ digital and print/ braille resources.

2. use the exclamation mark correctly in written exercises.

3. play games with peers that involve placing the exclamation mark correctly in a text.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. recognise the exclamation mark from writings on wall charts/ board/ digital and print/ braille resources.
2. use the exclamation mark correctly in written exercises.
3. play games with peers that involve placing the exclamation mark correctly in a text.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 10.4.1 Punctuation (The exclamation mark) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration is enhanced as the learner plays games with peers that involve placing the exclamation mark correctly in a text.

Values:
• Respect as the learner plays games that involve placing the exclamation mark correctly in a text.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self-esteem) -as the learner uses the exclamation mark correctly in writing.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The exclamation mark is learnt in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

• practice reading sentences with

• engage in timed reading of a text

feelings.

Core competencies to be developed:

• Self-efficacy; confidence and self-esteem are developed as a learner reads fluently.

• Digital literacy is enhanced as the learner participates in a reader’s theatre with peers and records on a digital device with assistive technology.

Values:

Responsibility as the learner takes charge of their own learning by reading accurately.

n) is enhanced as the learner plays word ladder games to practise correct pronunciation of words.
